item.title: Polls open in Israeli election seen as referendum on Netanyahu
item.description: Polls opened Tuesday in Israel’s critical national election viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s policies. Reporting from Jerusalem, FRANCE 24’s Noga Tarnopolsky explains that “the name of the game” after Election Day is whether the country’s fractious opposition, including an Arab-Israeli majority bloc, can come together to form a government.

item.title: How Trump’s ‘little detour’ to Iran became a roadblock in the midterm elections
item.description: When President Donald Trump launched his war on Iran, he said it would last a matter of weeks

item.title: Judge extends court-ordered block on Trump’s renovation plans for public golf course
item.description: A federal judge has agreed to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital

item.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Ballon d'Or
item.description: Kane was followed in the voting by Kylian Mbappé. Spain star Alexia Putellas won her third women's Ballon d'Or. Outside, fans packed the streets and climbed light poles near the London Palladium.

item.title: Trump and Rubio plan to visit oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude in Texas
item.description: President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio plan to showcase a newly arrived oil tanker filled with Venezuelan crude in Texas on Tuesday

item.title: Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show in Southern California
item.description: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are one victory from their first World Series title after routing the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night thanks to a trio of young players who have shined in October.

item.title: Local ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump starts in southern Ukraine
item.description: A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv.

item.title: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
item.description: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.

item.title: A quick guide to Israel's high-stakes elections
item.description: Israel is holding its first elections since the Hamas-led attacks of 2023 triggered a chain of conflicts across the region — a quick guide the key players, issues and when to expect a result.

item.title: Israel votes in first election since October 7 attack as Netanyahu faces crucial test
item.description: Israelis are voting Tuesday in the first general elections since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a fight for political survival. The vote follows three years of regional wars, with Netanyahu running neck and neck with centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot.

item.title: Kylian Mbappe loses two major China sponsorship deals over Mao Zedong joke
item.description: French football star Kylian Mbappe was dropped by two major Chinese brands on Tuesday after a video circulated online in which he appeared to joke about former leader Mao Zedong. Energy drink giant Dongpeng and dairy producer Mengniu said they had terminated their partnerships, citing remarks that offended Chinese national sentiment.

item.title: Users reporting problems with Apple's first foldable iPhone
item.description: Owners of Apple's first foldable iPhone have reported problems with the device's screen - just days after the product went on sale.

item.title: WATCH: Record early voting in key states as Trump, Obama appeal to voters on campaign trail
item.description: President Trump is campaigning in traditionally red states as voters worry about rising prices.

item.title: Jay-Z announced as Super Bowl LXI halftime show performer
item.description: Jay-Z is taking the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage. Super Bowl LXI will take place on Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Nurse treating Ebola patients killed by machete-wielding mob
item.description: A nurse responding to the Ebola outbreak it has been killed by a group of young people armed with machetes, officials have said.

item.title: Appeals court declines to step in on Trump administration's California voting case
item.description: Appeals court rejects DOJ request for immediate order demanding California segregate 20,000 mail-in ballots from those Trump administration says are likely non-citizens.

item.title: US-EU trade truce at risk over $3.4 billion Airbus loan, Trump official warns
item.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned on Monday that a $3.4 billion European Investment Bank loan to Airbus could jeopardise a tariff truce between Washington and Brussels. Greer said his office had received no details about the financing, announced in June, and urged the EU to resolve the matter quickly.

item.title: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
item.description: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information. Comey's lawyers immediately dismissed the effort as invalid and outside the time limit.

item.title: WATCH: Cruise liner collides with two docked cargo ships
item.description: Police in Germany say stormy weather caused the ship to drift toward the dock. No one was hurt.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro vows to lead opposition after Brazil court imposes travel ban
item.description: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Monday a Supreme Court justice had barred him from leaving the country after he narrowly lost to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro, who refused to concede defeat, denounced the order as intimidation and vowed to challenge the election results.

item.title: Harry Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or drought, Putellas wins third crown
item.description: Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season. Spain’s Alexia Putellas claimed her third women’s award after helping Barcelona win the Champions League, ending teammate Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign.

item.title: Europe's top NATO powers pledge greater defence role, reaffirm US alliance
item.description: Europe's five main NATO members said on Monday they were ready to take greater responsibility for the continent's security while reaffirming the United States as an "indispensable ally". Defence ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Poland and Britain pledged closer co-operation with Washington after talks in Paris on strengthening Europe's defence role.

item.title: Mecca pact nations hold talks with Iran to prevent renewed Middle East war
item.description: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks in Iran on Monday aimed at preventing renewed fighting in the Middle East, with Tehran describing discussions as “very good”. The diplomatic push, attended by Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, followed warnings from Washington, Tehran and Israel of renewed hostilities.

item.title: WATCH: Paris Hilton on navigating life after adult ADHD diagnosis
item.description: ABC News' Dr. Darien Sutton breaks down what you need to know about the disorder, and Paris Hilton shares more on her personal story.

item.title: Former FBI chief charged for third time by Trump administration
item.description: Former FBI chief James Comey has been charged for a third time by President Donald Trump's administration.

item.title: Protests in Europe: Fact-checking viral videos amid claims of 'chaos'
item.description: As young people protest poor school conditions and the rising cost of living across Europe, misleading videos are spreading online. Footage from Poland in 2017, military preparations in Portugal and a protest in Argentina have all been falsely presented as recent demonstrations in Europe, painting a misleading picture of unrest. Vedika Bahl fact-checks three viral videos to uncover what they really show and how old footage is recycled to spread misinformation and attract clicks.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows soaring sales and steep losses
item.description: AI giant Anthropic has publicly filed for an initial public offering (IPO) with US market regulators. The document offered a glimpse into the company's finances but also contained nearly 100 pages related to risks around investing in the company. The filing revealed that in the first half of 2026, its revenue soared to $16.3 billion while net loss widened to over $80 billion. Plus, London's iconic Oxford Street, one of Europe's busiest shopping areas, has been partially pedestrianised.

item.title: Serbia’s elections: 'Tracking fraud for sure had an impact on the results'
item.description: On October 25, Serbia's student-led protest movement won a historic victory in parliamentary ⁠elections, defeating outgoing President Aleksandar Vucic's party. Supporters of the student list explained to FRANCE 24 how they mounted a massive mobilisation to fight electoral fraud and monitor the electoral process inside and outside the polling stations.

item.title: The fall of El-Fasher, one year on
item.description: In tonight's edition, 15 military officials are sanctioned by the UK over the brutality and abuse of civilians during the fall of El Fasher. Also, ⁠Algeria's set to send in army units ​to ‌Niger ⁠to ‌protect energy ⁠and economic interests there. And days after a foreigner was beaten to death on the streets of Durban, the stalled asylum process has left many migrants living in fear.

item.title: Trump offers $1 million for tipoffs leading to vote fraud conviction as midterms approach
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday pledged a $1 million reward for information on voter fraud leading to conviction ahead of the upcoming 2026 US midterms on November 3. The president gave no details of how the reward would be funded or administered. The comments follow his repeated false claims that he won the 2020 presidential election.

item.title: Judge rules Trump DOJ 'unlawfully' fired Maurene Comey
item.description: A judge ruled against President Donald Trump and the DOJ over the firing of Maurene Comey from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Israel 'genocide' has continued in Gaza after ceasefire, UN report claims
item.description: Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza despite last October's ceasefire, a UN commission claims.

item.title: WATCH: Brad Raffensperger talks Georgia election security
item.description: Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger discusses election security and the political battle in the Peach State as Election Day nears.

item.title: When an invasive fish is also tasty, Maryland schoolkids can help 'eat the problem'
item.description: The Chesapeake Bay, home to blue crabs and striped bass, has a new apex predator: the blue catfish. It's invasive and voracious. It's also delicious, which officials hope might help save the bay.

item.title: Serbian student movement eyes power after election triumph
item.description: Emotions ran high in Belgrade on Monday after a student-led movement upset the right-wing populist Aleksandar Vucic's party in Serbia's snap election. A celebratory mood gripped the capital, with drivers honking their horns and passers-by holding up three fingers -- the winning list's ballot number and a Serbian greeting. Many wore badges and other symbols of the student movement, while a large group of residents spent the day cleaning up a park between parliament and the presidency after Vucic loyalists, who had camped there for more than a year, fled. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with researchers and political activist Aleksandar Matković.

item.title: Comeback kid: How did Brazil veteran-leader Lula upset Bolsonaro?
item.description: Two days shy of his 81st birthday… Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva emerging as the comeback kid. Coming from behind in the polls after a bitter campaign where he often showed his age, Lula becoming the first candidate since Brazil’s return to democracy in the 1980s to win the presidential runoff after trailing in the first round. How did the Workers Party leader turn a 2-point-2 million vote deficit against the far-right's Flavio Bolsonaro into a 4-point-4 million vote win? Reminder that three short weeks ago, most races at the federal and state level broke the way of conservatives and the far-right?

item.title: Teen pleads not guilty in hit-and-run that killed two 17-year-old girls on e-bike
item.description: Vincent Battiloro, 18, of Garwood, appeared in court for his arraignment on Monday, following his indictment this month on two counts of first-degree murder.

item.title: Trump administration pushes for food assistance card upgrade to fight fraud
item.description: The proposed rule is a major step forward in addressing a form of fraud that has robbed SNAP recipients of millions.

item.title: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
item.description: Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.

item.title: UN cites 'ethnic cleansing' concerns around Israel's Palestinian displacement operation in Hebron
item.description: The United Nations on Monday raised "ethnic cleansing" concerns following Israel's operation to displace by force more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron in the West Bank after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near the city on Friday. UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement that the "aggressive operation" must end, and that "collective punishment is a grave violation of international law".

item.title: French student union leaders call for 'continued mobilisation' after meeting PM
item.description: The French government met student representatives on Monday (October 26) following weeks of unrest. Students who had been demanding a meeting for weeks hail progress. Nonetheless they are now calling for fresh demonstrations next Saturday (October 31) to press for further measures. Details by FRANCE 24’s French Politics Editor Marc Perelman.

item.title: Trump told DOJ to sue to block Alaska Senate results if Republican narrowly loses
item.description: President Trump says he directed the DOJ to preemptively file a lawsuit to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses.

item.title: Brazil: What does Lula's re-election mean for the Amazon?
item.description: Climate activists in Brazil are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. His last four years in power saw a record decrease in deforestation in the world's largest rainforest.

item.title: Opponents accuse Netanyahu of stoking tensions with Iran before Israel's election
item.description: Israel's defence minister denied on Monday (October 26) reports of a rift between PM Netanyahu and the army over Iran, before the vote. Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, insisting only he can "finish the job" in the US-Israeli war on Iran. His main rival, ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, has accused him of playing up the Iran threat when it suits him politically, and of failing to accomplish his war goals. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Vatican issues Pope health update ahead of South America trip
item.description: The Pope is recovering well from cancer surgery and his trip to South America will go ahead as planned next month, the Vatican has said.

item.title: Leaders across Americas react to Brazil President Lula's re-election
item.description: ​President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential election on Sunday (October 25), defeating right-wing ​Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff to secure a fourth non-consecutive term.

item.title: Israeli candidate Eisenkot pledges to unite country as Netanyahu deems him 'soft' on Iran
item.description: Israeli presidential candidate Gadi Eisenkot's pledge made Sunday to "heal" Israeli society after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's divisive tenure resonated with some voters attending his final campaign rally before polling begins Tuesday. Netanyahu meanwhile received fresh backing for re-election from US President Donald Trump and deemed Eisenkot "soft" on Iran.

item.title: 'Lula accustomed to negotiating tough bargains': Campaign promises collide with right-wing Congress
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Christopher Sabatini, Director of Chatham House's Latin America Programme. Sabatini examines how Lula's campaign reinvention, youth mobilisation, and the changing dynamics of Bolsonarismo are reshaping Brazil's political landscape. By embracing social media, mobilising younger voters, and shifting attention from his historical achievements to the economic anxieties of ordinary Brazilians, Lula managed to transform the electoral contest. As Sabatini explains, voters were no longer satisfied with hearing about the past. They wanted an answer to a more immediate question: "What are you going to do for us now?

item.title: Israel election: unable to vote from abroad, expats have to fly home
item.description: Israelis can’t vote from abroad, so tens of thousands of expats are expected to fly home for the election. At Tel Aviv airport, supporters of opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot are already waiting at arrivals. A “Fly and Vote” initiative helps expats organise their trip, despite a failed petition from Netanyahu’s Likud party to restrict it. With polls predicting a tight race, every vote could count, and the result will decide the Prime Minister’s fate.
